newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus protesters blast referendum, Russia.
newsitem.headline: Belarus protesters blast referendum, Russia.

text.p: As many as 5,000 people turned out for a rally on Sunday in central Minsk to protest against a controversial referendum last month that gave sweeping powers to hardline Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko.

In the first major public show of opposition to the November 24 referendum which provided Lukashenko with a mandate to rewrite the constitution, an initial crowd of about 2,000 formed at midday at a central square opposite the parliament building.

Three thousand more, most of them young, joined the procession when the demonstrators, waving red-and-white national flags and chanting anti-presidential slogans, headed off towards Lukashenko's residence, watched by several hundred policemen.
"We will never accept the falsified constitution," Nikolai Statkevich, an organiser of the rally, said.
The protesters later halted near the Russian embassy and chanted slogans, including "Hands off Belarus" and "Shame on Russia", references to Moscow's acceptance of the referendum.

Belarus nationalists and other anti-Lukashenko groups resent the president's efforts to forge closer ties with Moscow. During the run-up to the referendum, Russia brokered a short-lived compromise deal between the president and his opponents.
A Reuter correspondent saw police detain six or seven protesters as the demonstration ended. However a police spokesman later denied any arrests had been made.
Organisers said further anti-Lukashenko demonstrations were planned for December 12 and December 25.

Lukashenko's referendum drew a barrage of criticism abroad. Last week a summit of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) in Lisbon said in a statement the referendum "was conducted in contradiction with constitutional procedures and cannot be considered as legitimate".
In a rare and public rebuke to a participating member, it told Lukashenko to ensure the freedom of the media, re-establish full democratic procedures and start talking to the opposition.
Lukashenko, 42, who also attended the Lisbon summit, shrugged off the criticism and told the 54-nation OSCE not to meddle in his country's affairs.

Within days of the referendum, he took steps to subdue any opposition to his rule. He has assembled a lower house composed entirely of his supporters and it promptly passed a law disbanding the old parliament headed by speaker Semyon Sharetsky, symbol of the president's domestic opposition.
Three judges of Belarus's 11-member Constitutional Court, including its head, resigned last week in protest against the referendum.
